problem.title: Design a 1M-Token Dynamic Context Management & Token Compression Engine
problem.tagline: Compressing 128k–1M token contexts to 8k–16k tokens in <500 ms p95 across 10,000 concurrent multi-tenant agent sessions.
problem.purpose: Design a distributed context management and dynamic token compression tier that eliminates 160 GB/session KV-cache bottlenecks, protects pinned system/tool anchors, isolates 10,000 tenants, and enforces >98% entity fact preservation.
problem.prompt: Design an enterprise Context Management & Dynamic Token Compression Engine handling 10,000 concurrent Agent/RAG sessions (1,000 turns/sec sustained), compressing 128k–1M token contexts down to 8k–16k tokens in <500 ms p95 with >98% reasoning and entity fact preservation.

prerequisites.title: Perplexity-Based Token Pruning & Anchor Pinning
prerequisites.summary: Know how 0.5B–1.5B INT8 SLMs score conditional surprisal I(x_i) and protect immutable Pinned Anchors.

prerequisites.title: Consistent Hashing & HMAC Tenant Isolation
prerequisites.summary: Understand how Session_ID hashing preserves KV-cache affinity and why HMAC-SHA256 key prefixing prevents cross-tenant bleed.

spark.summary: Route 10,000 sessions by Session_ID consistent hashing through SHA-256 Anchor Pinning, chunk-parallel INT8 SLM perplexity scoring, hierarchical summary trees in Redis L1 / NVMe RocksDB L2, and a 450 ms fail-open circuit breaker.
spark.keyTakeaway: When designing a 10,000-session 1M-token context compression platform under 500 ms p95, pair fixed-offset Pinned Anchors with parallel SLM perplexity pruning, HMAC-isolated L1/L2 summary trees, and a 450 ms fail-open circuit breaker.
spark.byteSummary:
At 10,000 concurrent agent sessions (1,000 turns/sec, 250k avg tokens/turn), raw LLM prefill would process 250M tokens/sec and consume up to 160 GB of FP16 KV cache per 1M-token 70B session—causing 18–35s Time-To-First-Token.

The RESHADED architecture decouples into five tiers: (1) Edge Gateway extracts and SHA-256-verifies Pinned Anchors (system prompts, tool schemas, safety rules) in <5 ms; (2) A fleet of 32–40 INT8 0.5B–1.5B SLM workers scores 62 parallel 4k chunks (128-token overlap) per turn in 90–120 ms p95; (3) Consistent-hashed Redis L1 (2.56 GB) and Zstd NVMe RocksDB L2 (40 GB/day) store 3-tier RAPTOR summary trees isolated by HMAC-SHA256(secret, tenant_id); (4) RadixAttention KV-affinity routing reuses pinned prefix blocks; (5) A 5% async shadow judge tunes threshold tau to hold >98% entity recall while a 450 ms circuit breaker fails open to a 12k raw tail.

Downstream LLM prefill drops 20.8x to 12M tokens/sec (>95% TCO savings) while keeping p95 compression + prefill under 500 ms.

learningJourney.title: R & E · Requirements, Little's Law & HBM Physics
learningJourney.whyThisMatters: Quantifies the 250M tok/s -> 12M tok/s reduction and Little's Law SLM GPU fleet sizing.

explanation.foundation: 10,000 concurrent sessions averaging 1 turn every 10s = 1,000 turns/sec (2,500 peak). At 250k avg tokens/turn, raw ingress is 250M tokens/sec.
explanation.core: Illustrative Sizing: Compressing to 12k tokens cuts downstream prefill to 12M tok/s (20.8x reduction). Splitting 250k tokens into 62 parallel 4k chunks scored in W = 90 ms yields L = 1,000 * 0.090 = 90 concurrent turns (~5,580 chunks) served by 32–40 INT8 L40S/H100 workers.
explanation.deepDive: Hot session state (16k active window + 64 KB summary tree + 128 KB metadata = 256 KB/session) totals 2.56 GB across 10k sessions—fitting in a 3-shard 16 GB Redis Cluster (RF=2).

learningJourney.title: S & H · Tiered Storage Schema & HMAC Tenant Isolation
learningJourney.whyThisMatters: Prevents cross-tenant KV-cache bleed while keeping session tree reads under 8 ms.

explanation.foundation: Multi-tenant RAG and agent platforms cannot share KV-cache prefixes or summary trees across organizations.
explanation.core: Every Redis L1 and NVMe RocksDB L2 key is prefixed with HMAC_SHA256(cluster_secret, tenant_id). RadixAttention blocks on GPU pods are tagged with (tenant_hmac, model_epoch, anchor_sha256).
explanation.deepDive: Cold 1M-token raw leaves are archived in Zstd-compressed S3/GCS partitions for 30 days, while 512-token branch nodes in NVMe RocksDB hold [ref:leaf_id] pointers for <8 ms drill-down.

learningJourney.title: A · Typed RPC Contract & Chronological Request Trace
learningJourney.whyThisMatters: Defines the exact 450 ms deadline-propagated contract and stage latency budgets.

explanation.foundation: The Compression Service exposes POST /v1/context/compress with X-Tenant-Id, X-Request-Deadline-Ms: 450, explicit anchors[], and context_segments[].
explanation.core: Stage budgets: Anchor Extract (<5 ms) -> Parallel SLM Perplexity (<120 ms) -> Tree Merge (<220 ms) -> Prefix-Stable Assembly (<350 ms) -> KV-Affine LLM Prefill (<480 ms p95).
explanation.deepDive: The response returns kv_affinity_pod_id so the API Gateway routes the compressed payload directly to the vLLM/SGLang pod holding warm RadixAttention blocks for that tenant's anchors.

learningJourney.codeExample:
def route_and_compress(tenant_id: str, session_id: str, anchors: list[str], segments: list[str], budget: int = 12288) -> dict:
    import hashlib, hmac
    tenant_hmac = hmac.new(b'cluster-secret', tenant_id.encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()[:16]
    cache_key = f'{tenant_hmac}:{session_id}'
    # 1. Verify anchor immutability
    anchor_digest = hashlib.sha256(('\n'.join(anchors)).encode()).hexdigest()
    return {
        'cache_key': cache_key,
        'anchor_digest': anchor_digest,
        'target_budget': budget,
        'deadline_ms': 450
    }

learningJourney.title: D & E · 3-3-3 Technology Trade-Offs & TCO Economics
learningJourney.whyThisMatters: Justifies INT8 SLM + Redis/RocksDB + H2O/RadixAttention over naive alternatives.

explanation.foundation: Without compression, 250M input tokens/sec costs ~$125/sec ($10.8M/day) in frontier prefill compute.
explanation.core: Compressing 20.8x to 12M tokens/sec cuts LLM prefill to ~$6.00/sec while the 40-GPU INT8 SLM fleet + Redis/RocksDB costs ~$0.04/sec—yielding >95% net TCO reduction.
explanation.deepDive: We pair H2O Heavy-Hitter KV eviction (retaining attention sinks 0..7 + heavy hitters) with RadixAttention prefix sharing rather than pure sliding-window eviction, which forgets mid-session entities.

decisionFramework.title: Architecture Trade-Off Checklist
criteria: Scorer: 0.5B–1.5B INT8 SLM (100 ms, 98.4% recall) beats BM25 (86% recall) and 7B LLM (800 ms).
Storage: Redis L1 + NVMe RocksDB L2 beats all-RAM Redis (30x cost) and SQL (raft write amp).
Verification: 5% async shadow judge beats 100% sync judge (0 ms hot-path penalty).

decisionExercise.prompt: The 5% async Shadow LLM Judge reports that entity recall for Tenant X dropped from 98.6% to 96.2% after a new verbose API log format rolled out. What should the Adaptive Controller do?

options.label: Disable compression globally for all 10,000 sessions
options.feedback: Disabling globally causes a 20x prefill cost and latency spike for healthy tenants.

options.label: Lower threshold tau by 15% (keep more tokens) and boost NER entity weights
options.feedback: Correct: closed-loop tau relaxation restores >98% recall within 60 seconds.

options.label: Delete Tenant X's Pinned Anchors to make room
options.feedback: Pinned Anchors are immutable and must never be deleted.

learningJourney.title: D · Failure Modes, Assumptions & Glossary
learningJourney.whyThisMatters: Ensures zero-downtime fail-open behavior, clear assumptions, and shared vocabulary.

explanation.foundation: Assumptions & Limitations: Assumes co-located SLM and LLM GPU pools in-region, 128k–1M input windows, and 8k–16k target budgets. Not suited for <8k prompts or verbatim legal redlines.
explanation.core: Failure Modes: (1) SLM fleet overload (>450 ms) trips Circuit Breaker OPEN to Pinned Anchors + 12k raw tail; (2) Redis L1 shard loss falls back to NVMe RocksDB L2 (+12 ms); (3) Anchor SHA-256 mismatch rejects with 403.
explanation.deepDive: Glossary: Pinned Anchor, Conditional Surprisal, Query-Contrastive PMI, Entropy-Retention Curve, Hierarchical Summary Tree, Attention Sink, Heavy-Hitter Token, RadixAttention, Boundary Stride Overlap, HMAC Tenant Prefixing, Shadow Judge, Adaptive tau, Fail-Open Breaker, Rehydration Pointer.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does a 1M-token session on a 70B FP16 GQA-8 model require ~160 GB of KV cache?

options.text: Because each token consumes ~160 KB of FP16 KV state across layers and heads
options.feedback: Correct: 1,000,000 * 160 KB = 160 GB, exceeding an 80 GB H100.

options.text: Because system prompts are stored in float64
options.feedback: Weights and KV caches use FP16/BF16/FP8, not float64.
KV cache lives in GPU HBM during inference.
Network buffers are kilobytes, not 160 GB.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Compressing 1M tokens to 12k tokens shrinks per-session KV cache from 160 GB to 1.92 GB (83x).

knowledgeChecks.question: How does the storage layer prevent Tenant A's prompt cache from leaking to Tenant B?

options.feedback: Persistence settings do not isolate in-memory keys.

options.text: By prefixing Redis/RocksDB keys with HMAC-SHA256(secret, tenant_id) and scoping RadixAttention blocks by tenant_hmac
options.feedback: Correct: cryptographic tenant scoping prevents key collisions and KV bleed.
Alphabetical sorting destroys semantic order and does not isolate tenants.
Transport protocol has no bearing on cache isolation.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: HMAC-SHA256 tenant prefixing isolates both L1/L2 storage and GPU RadixAttention KV blocks.

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the role of the [ref:leaf_id] pointer inside 512-token branch summary nodes?

options.text: It lets the assembler rehydrate raw 4k leaves from NVMe RocksDB in <8 ms when a new query matches an old branch
options.feedback: Correct: drill-down rehydration recovers exact verbatim details on demand.
It is a read pointer, not a deletion command.
Pinned Anchors always stay locked at the prefix.
It is a storage address pointer.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Rehydration pointers give O(log N) hierarchical drill-down without keeping 1M raw tokens in RAM.

knowledgeChecks.question: How many concurrent turns L are in flight on the SLM fleet at 1,000 turns/sec with W = 90 ms scoring latency?

options.feedback: Correct: by Little's Law L = lambda * W = 1,000 * 0.090 = 90.
10,000 is total active sessions, not simultaneous in-flight SLM turns.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Little's Law (L = lambda * W) sizes the INT8 SLM GPU worker pool at 32–40 GPUs with 40% headroom.

beginner.summary: Build a multi-layer compression gateway that locks system rules, trims filler with a tiny AI model, and stores old chat summaries on fast NVMe disks.
beginner.keyTakeaway: When scaling an AI platform to 10,000 long-context users, lock system rules first, compress history in parallel, and fall back safely if the compressor slows down.
beginner.byteSummary: Instead of sending 1M tokens to an expensive LLM every turn, this system locks system prompts, uses 40 small GPUs to prune filler words in 90 ms, stores old summaries in Redis/RocksDB, and fails open if latency spikes.

intermediate.summary: Consistent-hashed 10k-session compression tier using INT8 SLM perplexity scoring, Redis L1 + NVMe RocksDB L2 summary trees, and HMAC tenant isolation.
intermediate.keyTakeaway: When designing a 1M-token compression engine under 500 ms p95, shard sessions by HMAC tenant + session_id, score 4k chunks in parallel, and guard latency with a 450 ms fail-open breaker.
intermediate.byteSummary: By combining SHA-256 Pinned Anchors, 62-chunk parallel SLM scoring (L=90 concurrent turns), and H2O/RadixAttention KV-cache reuse, the platform cuts prefill volume 20.8x and TCO >95% while maintaining >98% entity recall.

advanced.summary: Full RESHADED architecture: deterministic anchor pinning, 128-stride chunk-parallel SLM surprisal + query PMI, RAPTOR trees, H2O + tenant-scoped RadixAttention, and 5% async shadow PID control.
advanced.keyTakeaway: When designing a 10,000-session 1M-token context compression platform under 500 ms p95, pair fixed-offset Pinned Anchors with parallel SLM perplexity pruning, HMAC-isolated L1/L2 summary trees, and a 450 ms fail-open circuit breaker.
advanced.byteSummary: Reduces 70B FP16 KV-cache footprint from 160 GB to 1.92 GB/session (83x) and raw ingress from 250M to 12M tok/s across 32–40 INT8 SLM GPUs, with 2.56 GB Redis L1, Zstd NVMe RocksDB L2, and closed-loop 5% shadow drift governance.
